title: Payer Offset and Recoupment Radar
one_liner: Reconstruct the silent payer clawbacks buried in the 835 provider-level adjustment segment, then dispute the ones that lack notice or exceed state look-back limits.
customer: Community and mid-size hospitals, physician groups and MSOs, and RCM outsourcers who want a recovery line item. SaaS at $1-3k/month, or 15-25% of reversed recoupments.
problem: Payers increasingly claw money back by netting it inside the electronic remittance (835) PLB provider-level balance segment, or by short-paying unrelated claims. These adjustments carry cryptic reason codes and no patient or claim detail. Cash posters drop them into a suspense or 'other adjustment' account, or write them off. The overpayment letters that justify them arrive by mail, fax or random emails and are never matched. Many states cap retroactive recoupment look-back windows and require claim-level notice, but no one checks whether the payer complied.
solution: Ingest 12-24 months of 835s and the payer's overpayment and audit letters (PDF/email/fax OCR). Rebuild every offset to claim level. Flag recoupments with no valid notice, past the state or contract look-back, duplicating a prior recoupment, or hitting claims already appealed. Generate dispute letters and track outcomes. A payer scorecard shows clawback dollars per $1M paid, which gives the CFO leverage at contract renewal.
why_now: Payer payment-integrity programs are scaling with AI-driven post-payment audits and coding-policy downcodes. Medicare Advantage audit pressure is rising. Hospitals staffed thin after the 2025-26 Medicaid and margin squeeze cannot chase each offset by hand. Post-payment recoupment is the fastest-growing part of the denial problem and the least instrumented.
revenue_model: Contingency 15-25% of recoupments reversed, or $1-3k/month per facility for monitoring plus a $5-10k onboarding audit. Payer scorecards can be sold to hospital associations.
non_obvious_insight: Denial management tools watch denied claims. Recoupments are not denied claims. They are negative dollars in the remit file that nobody owns. Only cash posters see them and they are told to just post them. In a typical mid-size hospital these unmatched offsets total mid-six to seven figures a year, and dispute success is highest exactly where the payer skipped required notice. The data is already sitting in files the hospital owns.
first_30_days: Ask 5 friendly hospital and group cash-posting managers for 12 months of 835s (clearinghouses can export them), which requires only a BAA. Write a parser for the PLB segments (about a week of work) and produce a 'recoupment leakage report' showing unmatched offset dollars per payer. Use the number to sign 2 contingency pilots, and build the letter-matching module on real customer data.

title: Cloud-Bricking Escrow for Hardware Brands
one_liner: A neutral escrow-and-standby service that holds a hardware brand's cloud backend and local-mode firmware, and takes over the moment the cloud vendor fails.
customer: Consumer-hardware brands that outsource their cloud or app to an ODM or startup: private-label and licensed smart-home, router, EV-charger, pet-tech and e-bike brands. Retailers and insurers are secondary buyers.
problem: When a small backend vendor dies, the brand that sold the device takes the blame. Motorola-branded routers stopped being manageable when the MotoSync+ app failed. Play Store reviews say a third-party backend host's licence expired and the host ended operations ('Server Licence Expired'). Users report months without a fix. Spotify Car Thing became 'a $200 hardware turned into e-waste overnight.' An HN commenter estimated $300k-600k to open-source a single project, so afterthought rescue is unaffordable.
solution: For a flat annual fee, the brand deposits its backend container images and infrastructure-as-code, sealed secrets, signed 'local mode' firmware or companion-app builds, and device protocol docs. The operator monitors cloud health, domain and cert expiry, app-store status and vendor solvency signals. On a trigger it either runs the backend on standby infrastructure (pay-per-device) or releases the local-mode build. Brands that certify get an 'Afterlife Ready' mark for retail listings and regulator conversations.
why_now: EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations began on 11 Sept 2026, with full manufacturer obligations from 11 Dec 2027 and lifecycle handling required. Startup shutdowns are running at a high rate: 14.4% of H1 2026 shutdowns were AI companies with a median age of 2.3 years and a median $30k cash at closure. Recent bricking cases (Motorola routers in Jun 2026, Nest thermostats, Kodak Pulse frames, Samsung fridges in Sept 2026) are fresh in retailers' minds.
revenue_model: $5-25k/yr escrow subscription per brand, plus $0.10-0.50/device/month for hot standby and a per-incident recovery fee. Certification audits are a later add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The liability chain runs from a dead vendor through the brand to the customer, and existing escrow (software licence escrow, to my knowledge) is not built for live device fleets. Evidence: the Motorola router thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48425611, 238 points) traces the outage to a third-party server licence expiring after the host company ended operations. The 'when hardware goes EOL' essay (https://www.marcia.no/words/eol; HN discussion at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46609492, 403 points) lists Nest, Car Thing and Kodak Pulse. It quotes the $300k-600k open-sourcing estimate and community workarounds (OpenWRT, 'No Longer Evil'). The EU CRA page (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act) sets the 11 Sept 2026 and 11 Dec 2027 dates. The buyer is the brand, not the consumer, and the fee has to be cheaper than a single recall.
first_30_days: Week 1: build a free 'BackendWatch' monitor that pings a brand's cloud endpoints, cert expiry and domain renewals. Week 2: cold-email 50 licensed-brand and private-label hardware companies, and Kickstarter-scale hardware founders. Weeks 3-4: sign 3 design partners on a $2.5k pilot escrow. Write the trigger contract with a startup-insolvency lawyer.

title: Chip-to-Billet Solid-State Metal Mini-Mills
one_liner: Turn aluminum machining chips directly into billet, rod or wire by friction extrusion, with no remelting, first as a tolling service and then as on-site micro-mills.
customer: Aerospace, defense and precision machine shops with segregated 6061 and 7075 chips, plus extruders and AM wire makers who want recycled content.
problem: Machining chips sell for a fraction of ingot value and are remelted with real melt loss and energy. Aerospace buy-to-fly waste is huge, and domestic aluminum is exposed to tariffs and supply shocks.
solution: Solid-state processing (friction or shear-assisted extrusion, developed at national labs) consolidates single-alloy chips into bar or wire feedstock, preserving alloy chemistry. Phase 1 is a tolling service: ship chips in, get billet back. Phase 2 is a leased on-site mini-mill.
why_now: Tariffs on imported aluminum rose to 50% in mid-2025 and defense and aerospace capacity is stretched. Solid-state processes moved from lab demos toward pilots, so a first product now exists.
revenue_model: Tolling fee per pound returned, then equipment lease plus per-pound fee, plus recycled-content premiums.
non_obvious_insight: Melting destroys the metallurgical history. Chips from a single-alloy shop are effectively pre-alloyed, so solid-state consolidation captures value that a remelt discards.
first_30_days: Partner with a national lab or press builder. Run sample consolidations on chips from 3 shops and test tensile properties. Sell pilot lots to 2 extruders. Apply for AFWERX or SBIR support.

title: Human-Backed Login for Senior-Serving Software
one_liner: A drop-in login layer for apps whose users are 65+ that replaces passwords with a two-tap flow, a spoken one-time code by phone call (landline included), family delegates and a live concierge who can walk anyone in.
customer: Vertical SaaS vendors whose users are older adults: senior-living and home-care family portals, community and church software, benefits and Medicare-broker portals, pharmacy and telehealth apps, funeral-planning tools. They pay about $0.80-2 per active senior per month, $3 per concierge-assisted login, with a $299/month minimum.
problem: An operator of a ~10-year-old SaaS used heavily by people 65+ says users 'are tired and frustrated about remembering the domain/path to login screen and then which email/password they used', and that simplification has not fixed it. The 60 responses show what fails: forced resets, masked passwords, magic links (older users struggle switching apps), QR codes and passkeys. What people say they'd pay for is a human: 'elderly individuals want a solution rather than a lesson', and a 'code that you can type in on another device... my grandmother could call and read me a code'.
solution: Per-customer short vanity login URL plus a large 'Call me' button that triggers a phone call reading a short code aloud, working for landlines and flip phones, then persistent trusted-device sessions that effectively never log out. A family-delegate approve/reset flow, no forced password rotation, and no masked fields by default. When automation fails, a live concierge line verifies identity via vendor-supplied challenge questions and completes recovery. Ship as an SDK/widget plus hosted pages, with audit logs suitable for HIPAA-adjacent customers, and report the reduction in login-related support tickets per customer.
why_now: Big platforms pushed passkeys to consumers in 2025-2026 and older users, and the relatives who support them, are loudly reporting confusion and lockouts. The same vendors are under pressure to support MFA. Telephony APIs make voice-delivered codes cheap, and support cost per senior user is the metric operators feel.
revenue_model: Per-active-senior monthly fee, per-assisted-login fee for concierge calls, $299/month minimum, and an annual contract with an ticket-reduction guarantee for larger vendors.
non_obvious_insight: Authentication products optimize against attackers; for the 65+ user the dominant failure is support cost and churn, and the operators in the thread say the answer they would pay for is a human plus a code they can read out loud, not a better protocol. Every fashionable option (passkeys, magic links, QR) was named as failing for this group in the same thread. Evidence: Ask HN 'Easiest UX for Seniors', 58 points, 60 comments https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47729327; passkey confusion for elderly relatives and recovery gaps https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49010448.
first_30_days: Wire Twilio Verify's voice channel to a hosted 'Call me to log in' page and staff a three-person phone shift. Pitch 20 founders of senior-vertical SaaS (found via LinkedIn and association vendor directories), starting with the Ask HN author. Offer a $299/month 60-day pilot that measures login-related support tickets before and after, and convert on a shown reduction.

title: By Heart: Memorization Recitals as Status
one_liner: A membership club where knowledge workers memorize whole works and perform them at ticketed, witnessed recital nights, making 'held in my head' the new marathon medal.
customer: Affluent 28-55 year old knowledge workers (lawyers, designers, engineers, execs) who feel their minds going soft from AI offloading. Secondary buyers are hosts who want a 'living book' at a dinner, and companies booking offsites.
problem: Retrieval and summarization are now free and instant, so 'I know X' signals nothing. Bodies have legible, socially rewarded proof of discipline (marathons, Whoop scores, Hyrox). Minds have none. The 'cognitive debt' discourse around AI use is producing anxiety, but there is no communal, visible way to do something about it.
solution: 8-week cohorts with a memory coach and a deliberately text-hiding spaced-repetition app (no AI recall aids). A 'Canon' of about 60 pieces: sonnets, a Rilke elegy, Book IV of the Aeneid in translation, the Gettysburg Address, a language's 500 proverbs. Progress levels (100 lines, 500, 1,000, a whole play). Each level ends in a public recital in a bar or library, with two strangers in the audience co-signing a 'Held' certificate. A leaderboard tracks lines held. High-tier patrons book private salons where a member recites at dinner.
why_now: By 2026 the MIT Media Lab 'Your Brain on ChatGPT' study and the 'cognitive debt' idea have become mainstream (Psychology Today, Substack, Medium), and poetry-memorization essays are circulating as a counter-movement. Chat agents now do everything except being you. Run clubs, pickleball, and social-fitness scenes show demand for communal costly-signal hobbies. Nobody has built the cognitive equivalent.
revenue_model: $45/month membership. $199 cohort fees. $25-40 recital tickets. $1,500-5,000 for private 'living book' salons. $8-15k corporate offsite packages. Later, certified coach licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Status flows to whatever is costly, public, and impossible to outsource. Memory just became that, the way running became status once cars made walking optional. The proof is a witnessed live performance, which AI cannot fake and which needs no equipment, so it is a democratic status game with a cheap entry fee.
first_30_days: Run three free recital nights at a bar or library in one city and recruit about 20 people. Pre-sell a 6-week $199 cohort. Recruit 2-3 theater or memory-sport coaches on rev-share. Run everything on Notion and an existing flashcard tool. Target 30 paid members and 2 private salon bookings by day 90.

title: Lead-Refund Recovery for Home-Service Pros
one_liner: Auto-dispute junk paid leads from Google Local Services, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp, and take a share of the credits recovered.
customer: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, locksmith, garage-door, pest and electrical firms with 3-30 employees spending $2k-30k a month on paid leads.
problem: A large share of paid leads are spam, wrong-service, out-of-area or duplicates (typically cited at 20-40%; prior knowledge). Disputes are manual and deadline-bound, so owners rarely file. Getting customers is the top small-business challenge, so the spend is untouchable but the waste is fixable.
solution: Connect ad and lead accounts and the phone system's call recordings. Transcribe and classify each lead against each platform's dispute reasons, file disputes with evidence inside the window, track credits, and flag chronically junky sources. A monthly report shows net cost per real lead.
why_now: Cheap call transcription and LLM classification make per-lead review nearly free, and legacy local-marketing vendors are shrinking and raising prices, which raises the value of every recovered credit.
revenue_model: 20-25% of credits recovered (no credit, no fee), or $99/month per account.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody sells lead-refund recovery because each dispute is worth $30-150, but automation turns them into a portfolio. Recovered credits are pure margin for the owner.
first_30_days: Ask 10 contractors from local trade Facebook groups for 90 days of lead exports and call logs. File disputes manually to learn acceptance rates, then automate the top three reason codes.

title: Parametric Cover Against Career-Field Collapse
one_liner: Index-based protection that pays out when hiring in a specific occupation falls past a threshold, sold first to bootcamps, income-share funds and private student lenders whose job-guarantee promises are now correlated bets on entry-level demand.
customer: Bootcamps with job guarantees, ISA funds, private student lenders and university tuition-protection programs. Later, workers via employers and universities as a benefit.
problem: These institutions underwrite outcomes assuming stable entry-level demand. If CS, marketing or analytics hiring drops 30% they all fail together, and no hedge exists. The tail risk is now visible (22-25-year-olds in exposed jobs 19% below trend, junior tech postings down ~35% in major EU countries in 2024).
solution: Phase 1 (about 6 months): publish an Occupation Demand Index (postings, hires, claims mix by occupation and metro) plus stress-test analytics, sold as a subscription to lenders and ISA funds. Phase 2: structure parametric covers through an MGA, fronting carrier and reinsurers, triggered by the index. Phase 3: consumer livelihood cover via employers and universities.
why_now: Occupation-level posting data (e.g. Indeed Hiring Lab) is rich, AI exposure is a new correlated risk, parametric insurance infrastructure has matured, ISA funds and bootcamps are under strain, and event-contract markets are normalised.
revenue_model: Analytics subscriptions ($30-120k a year) first, then premiums and ceding commissions.
non_obvious_insight: Occupational risk has never been hedged because individual triggers create moral hazard. An index solves that for institutions whose portfolio effectively is the occupation, and AI displacement is exactly the correlated tail that reinsurers price.
first_30_days: Build the index from public BLS and posting data and backtest against bootcamp outcome reports. Pitch 10 ISA funds, bootcamps and private lenders a paid $10-25k stress-test pilot.

title: L-Band Radar Watchdog for Small Levee Districts
one_liner: Turn free NISAR L-band radar into monthly, engineer-stamped settlement and seepage alerts for the small local districts that own most of America's levees.
customer: Reclamation, levee and drainage districts (California Delta and Central Valley, Iowa/Illinois/Missouri/Arkansas drainage districts) and owners of small high-hazard earthen dams and irrigation canals. Budgets are $50k to $2M a year, run by a board plus a part-time manager.
problem: Grass-covered earthen levees lose coherence in C-band InSAR (Sentinel-1), so cheap remote settlement monitoring never worked on them. Districts rely on annual walk-through inspections by volunteers or consultants. Failures are catastrophic, and grant, subvention and insurance paperwork demands documented condition history that most districts lack.
solution: A pipeline on NISAR L-band (about 10 m, 12-day repeat, which sees through vegetation) plus Sentinel-1 and soil-moisture change. It produces per-levee-mile maps of slumping, settlement and unusual wetness (seepage proxy). Alerts go to a partner licensed geotechnical engineer, who signs a one-page condition letter. The district attaches that letter to state levee-subvention and federal rehabilitation-program files, insurer renewals and board minutes. The dashboard is secondary; the stamped trigger is the product.
why_now: NASA/ISRO began releasing NISAR L-band data free through ASF DAAC on July 20, 2026 (acquisitions from June 17, 2026; full science record due by end of 2026). Tens of thousands of levee miles are locally owned, and nobody had L-band time series at this cadence before. Whoever starts the baseline now owns the longest history.
revenue_model: Subscription of $3k to $8k a year per district, tiered by levee miles. Add $1.5k to $4k per engineer-stamped event report. Later, portfolio-level data licences to flood insurers and reinsurers, and to state agencies that fund many districts.
non_obvious_insight: The radar data is free and commoditizing, so the data is not what the customer buys. They buy a defensible, professionally signed trigger that unlocks grant money, satisfies insurers and shifts liability. The moat is the engineer-of-record relationship, local ground truth and a baseline archive that starts accumulating today.
first_30_days: Process Sentinel-1, ALOS-2 and the first NISAR stacks over one Delta island or Iowa drainage district with a known past slump, to show a retrospective catch. Sign a geotech firm as engineer of record. Offer 5 districts a free baseline map and a $1.5k pilot, pitched at levee-district association and flood-board meetings. Aim for 2 paid pilots by day 30.

title: Medicaid Look-Back Packet Builder
one_liner: Turn 60 months of messy bank statements into a caseworker-ready Medicaid application packet with explanations, so families avoid 'failure to provide verification' denials.
customer: Adult children and POA agents applying for nursing-home Medicaid for a parent ($299-$499 per case), plus elder-law and Medicaid-planning firms and senior placement advisors ($500-$1,500/month seats or per-case fees).
problem: Long-term-care Medicaid reviews up to 60 months of statements for every open account and every account closed within the window. Caseworkers typically demand written explanations for each expenditure over about $500. If records are missing the application is likely denied for 'failure to provide verification'. POA agents often lack online access to old or closed accounts, and banks can charge research fees for paper copies. Meanwhile the parent's care bills accumulate and elder-law attorneys charge thousands.
solution: Upload statements (PDF, CSV or bank link) and use OCR and an LLM to build the ledger. Detect large transfers, gifts, transfers to relatives and round-number withdrawals. Show likely penalty-period exposure. Draft the explanation letters and a caseworker index with state-specific checklists. Auto-generate missing-statement request letters to banks with a POA cover page, track which accounts are still missing, and hand the attorney a clean exception report. A separate 'consolidate and simplify before you need Medicaid' mode targets families planning ahead.
why_now: Document extraction and bank-data aggregation now make a 60-month review a minutes-long task rather than paralegal hours. Federal law (H.R. 1) sets a $1M Medicaid home-equity cap from Jan 1, 2028, and the 2026 baseline is $752,000 in most states, so more middle-class families in expensive housing markets will need spend-down or planning. State caseworkers will also be stretched by the 2027 work-requirement rollout, making complete first-time packets more valuable.
revenue_model: $299-$499 per family packet, $99 'look-back risk scan' as a lead magnet, and $500-$1,500/month firm seats or $75-$150 per case for elder-law offices, with placement-advisor referral fees as a secondary channel.
non_obvious_insight: The denial reason is paperwork, not eligibility: the requirement to explain each $500+ transaction and produce statements for closed accounts is a software-shaped burden that elder-law attorneys currently bill by the hour. See the documentation rules and 'likely deny for failure to provide verification' language at https://www.paelderlaw.net/medicaid-application-process-5-year-look-back-5-years-of-records-for-small-and-inactive-accounts/. The home-equity change is at https://justiceinaging.org/hr1-imposes-new-limit-on-home-equity-for-medicaid-ltss-effective-2028/. Bank refusal to deal with POA agents compounds it (https://www.aarp.org/caregiving/financial-legal/power-of-attorney-bank-approval/). Reddit was unreachable, so this rests on legal-practice and AARP sources describing the recurring r/AgingParents 'Mom needs Medicaid, what do they want?' situation.
first_30_days: Start with one state with clear caseworker checklists (Pennsylvania or New York). Hand-build 5 packets for free for local elder-law paralegals to validate the exception logic, then productize statement parsing and letter generation. Sell a $99 risk scan and a $349 packet through caregiver Facebook groups and 3-5 elder-law and placement-advisor partners, aiming for 10 paid packets and one firm pilot.

title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for Downstream Payers
one_liner: Recover itemized tariff surcharges from suppliers who were refunded the tariffs, on contingency, and give surcharge-collecting firms a defensive ledger.
customer: Small contractors, restaurants, repair shops and retailers who were invoiced a separate 'tariff surcharge' line by suppliers in 2025-26, plus small firms that added such surcharges to their own customers' bills.
problem: SCOTUS ruled on 2026-02-20 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, and about $166B in CBP refunds go to the importer of record (about $81B paid by July). Over 40% of small firms saw tariff cost increases and 76% of international sourcers passed them on, so the firm that paid the pass-through gets nothing. Each claim is too small ($200-$8k) for a lawyer, and firms that billed surcharges to their own customers now carry their own exposure.
solution: Read-only scan of the owner's mailbox and QuickBooks/Xero pulls every tariff or surcharge line from vendor invoices and from the firm's own customer invoices. It builds a two-sided surcharge ledger (paid upstream, collected downstream), then generates supplier demand letters that cite the invoice wording and contract terms. Unpaid claims escalate to small-claims templates or a partner attorney. Claims are strongest where the invoice said the surcharge was itemized or refundable. Because one supplier can owe hundreds of customers, settlements can be negotiated per supplier instead of per claim.
why_now: Refunds have been flowing through CBP's automated system since April 2026, so suppliers are holding refund cash right now, before it is absorbed into margins. Invoice records are fresh and 2026 books have not closed.
revenue_model: 25-30% contingency on recovered dollars, with a $49 flat fee for the ledger and audit. Later, a per-supplier settlement-program fee.
non_obvious_insight: Refund law is written for importers, but the money trail is an invoice trail. Itemized invoices are contract evidence, and thousands of tiny claims against a few hundred suppliers form a portfolio no law firm will touch. The same ledger doubles as a defense file for firms that billed surcharges.
first_30_days: Offer a free 'surcharge audit' in trade-specific Facebook groups and subreddits (HVAC, restaurant equipment, apparel resellers). Hand-review 50 mailboxes and find the 10 suppliers with the most itemized surcharges. Retain a consumer-protection attorney to review the demand-letter template, send the first 100 letters, and measure the response rate.

title: Vetted Remote Operators for Home Robots
one_liner: A privacy-audited, background-checked, insured pool of remote operators who take over home and warehouse robots at their hard moments, sold to robot makers as the trust layer for teleoperation.
customer: Home-robot, service-robot and warehouse-robot makers pay $18-35 per operator-hour. Operators are displaced support and ops workers earning $22-30 an hour.
problem: The first consumer humanoids (such as 1X's NEO) ship in 2026 relying on remote humans who can see inside homes, which raised a privacy backlash. Robot startups lack a scalable, vetted, insured operator workforce and would otherwise use anonymous offshore BPOs, while buyers want accountable domestic operators.
solution: Recruit and train from displaced call-centre, ops and gaming talent. A standard teleop certification, privacy protocols (blurred or avatarised feeds, no recording, no-go zones), session audit logs, background checks and E&O/cyber insurance form the service. Scheduling covers time zones and performance metrics track intervention success. Start with warehouse or delivery robots, then homes.
why_now: Consumer humanoid preorders and shipments began in 2025-26 with teleop as the fallback, warehouse and sidewalk robots are at scale, and privacy concerns make trust a differentiator.
revenue_model: 30-40% margin per operator-hour, certification fees and an insurance premium share.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for robots is not hardware but trusted remote labor, and every teleop intervention also trains the policy. Privacy trust, not price, is the moat, and it reframes displaced workers as a new 'robot pilot' class.
first_30_days: Contact 20 robotics startups (delivery, warehouse, cleaning) with a pilot of 5 vetted operators for 200 hours at cost. Write the privacy protocol and audit template. Recruit 30 candidates from laid-off support and ops staff.

title: AI Coverage Buy-Back Packs for Insurance Agents
one_liner: An intake that turns a small business's AI usage into an underwriter-ready 'AI use and guardrails' package so its insurer will restore the coverage it just excluded.
customer: Independent insurance agencies and brokerages that serve SMBs, who pay per client pack or a monthly agency subscription. Their clients are marketing agencies, law and accounting firms, clinics, staffing firms and e-commerce brands that use AI heavily.
problem: ISO endorsements CG 40 47 and CG 40 48 took effect in January 2026 and let carriers exclude generative-AI-related bodily injury, property damage and advertising injury from standard general liability policies. Reporting says Chubb, Travelers and Berkshire Hathaway got state approvals, and more than 80% of such requests were approved. Absolute AI exclusions are also appearing on D&O and E&O policies, including for 'allegedly inadequate AI governance'. About 74% of small businesses already use AI tools, and agents cannot tell clients what evidence underwriters will accept.
solution: A 15-minute intake, plus an optional SSO or browser scan, inventories the client's AI tools. It maps each use (customer chatbot, AI-generated ads, AI hiring screens, AI note-takers with client data) to the coverage lines it touches. It then produces: (1) a coverage-gap report that flags CG 40 47/48 and absolute AI exclusions in the current policy, (2) an underwriter-ready AI use and guardrails statement with a human-review log and vendor list, and (3) a quote-request package aimed at markets that sell affirmative AI coverage or buy-backs. Every pack also gives the agent a talk track for the renewal meeting.
why_now: The exclusions have been in effect since January 2026 and are now hitting renewals. Search interest is rising in the underlying concepts: Exploding Topics shows AI Guardrails +8,400%, Responsible AI +3,600% and Cyber Insurance +763%. Colorado's AI Act, delayed to Jan 1, 2027, and Illinois HB 3773 (in effect Jan 1, 2026) add employer-side documentation duties that the same pack can reuse.
revenue_model: $149-$299 per client pack, or $199-$499/month per agency for unlimited packs plus renewal reminders. Later: a referral or placement fee from managing general agents and carriers that write AI buy-backs, and a co-branded version sold through carrier appointment programs.
non_obvious_insight: The evidence standard does not exist yet. Law firm analyses of the exclusions note they 'stop short of prescribing specific governance standards insurers will accept' (https://www.lathropgpm.com/insights/the-ai-coverage-gap-what-new-insurance-exclusions-mean-for-your-business/) and describe fragmenting coverage across GL, D&O, E&O and EPLI (https://www.fenwick.com/insights/publications/end-silent-ai-emerging-ai-exclusions-coverage-fragmentation-and-practical-implications). Whichever evidence format two or three underwriters or MGAs accept first will become the SOC 2 of AI coverage. Agents, not the businesses themselves, are the right buyer because they lose commission if a client goes bare. Cyber-insurance search interest is up 763% and AI Guardrails up 8,400% (https://explodingtopics.com/finance-topics, https://explodingtopics.com/blog/trending-topics), which shows SMBs are already looking for this without a product to buy.
first_30_days: Days 1-10: build the intake form and PDF generator, and interview 15 independent agents (local IIABA and Big I chapters, LinkedIn) about how renewals with AI exclusions are being handled. Days 11-20: run free packs for each agent's five most AI-heavy clients, and ask two MGA underwriters whether the format is acceptable. Days 21-30: start charging $149 per pack. Target 5 agencies at $199/month and post 'we got X's AI coverage bought back' cases from the pilots.

title: Live-Action Fraud Drills Using Immersive Theater
angle: Pairing 2: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms x Cybersecurity, deepfake fraud, identity verification, scams targeting consumers and businesses
one_liner: Ticketed and B2B immersive-theater experiences where participants, with consent, get scammed by actors and voice-cloned 'relatives' in a safe space and learn the tells under real emotional pressure.
customer: Credit unions, community banks and insurers that want measurable fraud-loss reduction among older customers; employers' security teams and finance, HR and IT-helpdesk staff (named targets of voice deepfakes); senior-living operators, libraries and AARP-style chapters. Escape-room and immersive-theater operators are licensees.
problem: Per the briefing, adults 60+ lost $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), account for 66% of crypto-ATM losses, and law-enforcement-impersonation scams produced about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B+ with fake video calls. Conventional awareness training (videos, phishing simulations) shows little measurable effect; a 2025 study of about 19,500 UCSD Health employees found annual training had almost no impact on click rates (verify). Voice cloning now needs only 3 seconds of audio. The pressure tactics (urgency, secrecy, authority) are exactly what a lecture cannot simulate.
solution: A repeatable, franchisable 60-90 minute experience. Participants get a 'phone call' from an actor-controlled voice clone of a consenting volunteer (real-time voice conversion trained on the volunteer's own sample) or a fake CFO. They move through an escalating fraud script (fake bank, 'police', crypto-ATM instructions) with hidden facilitators, then a debrief teaches three tells and sets up a family or team safe-word protocol. Each participant leaves with a personalised safe-word card and help turning on their bank's trusted-contact feature. A B2B mobile 30-minute 'CFO voice-clone drill' scores the sponsor on how many people stop the transfer at each step. Outcomes are measured pre/post and at 90 days. Psychological-safety protocol and a counselor are built in.
why_now: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, when awareness budgets are spent. The FBI's 17 Sep 2026 PSA cites AI video calls in law-enforcement impersonation. Real-time voice conversion is cheap and voice-deepfake attacks are surging. Regulators are pushing banks to protect vulnerable customers (for example the UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement since Oct 2024), so banks want provable prevention.
revenue_model: Sponsors pay $3-8k per community event of 30-60 participants, or $40-150 per employee for corporate drills. Licensing or franchise fees from venues (about $1.5k/month plus event share). Public ticketed shows at $25-40 with sponsor underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud victims are not ignorant. They are overwhelmed by staged emotion under time pressure, and skills learned in calm classrooms fail under stress. Live-experience designers know how to induce and safely release exactly that state, and security teams know the real scripts. Banks can also compute ROI in avoided losses, which theater companies cannot.
first_30_days: Pair an immersive-theater company with a fraud investigator. Prototype a 45-minute 'grandparent scam' and a 'CFO deepfake' scenario with consent forms and a licensed counselor. Pilot with two credit unions and one library during October at about $2.5k each. Measure pre/post behavior with a follow-up test call. Use results to sell to regional credit-union leagues and security-awareness teams.

title: Heirloom Fair-Division Engine for Sibling Estates
one_liner: Use a fair-division algorithm and a phone walkthrough to split a dead parent's belongings so nobody feels cheated.
customer: Executors (often the eldest child), estate attorneys, mediators and professional fiduciaries. Families pay $149-$399 per estate, or attorneys pay $99/month.
problem: Research on inheritance conflict (for example the University of Minnesota's 'Who Gets Grandma's Yellow Pie Plate?' work) finds sentimental personal property, not money, triggers most sibling fights. Executors improvise with turn-taking or a spreadsheet, distant siblings get shortchanged, and the house can't be sold until it is cleared.
solution: A phone walkthrough captures the house room by room, AI tags items, and each remote heir gets a private points budget to express wants. A fair-division algorithm (adjusted-winner or envy-free-up-to-one-item style) proposes an allocation with cash or point equalization. The app then coordinates shipping and pickup, and routes leftovers to donation with receipts or to sale. It ends with a signed distribution memo the attorney can file. Each item keeps a story card so its history survives.
why_now: Multimodal AI can inventory objects from video, and phone-based 3D capture is mainstream. Boomer households hold decades of belongings that Millennial and Gen X heirs scattered across the country often don't want. With the federal estate tax largely out of the picture for most families (reported $15M exemption), family conflict is the main remaining risk.
revenue_model: Per-estate fee ($149-$399), 10-15% margin on shipping and donation logistics, and attorney seats at $99/month.
non_obvious_insight: The fights are about objects, not dollars. Objects are one of the few asset classes with a known mechanism-design solution, and no estate product uses it.
first_30_days: Build a no-code prototype with a spreadsheet points auction. Offer it free to 20 executors found in estate-help forums and groups. Ask elder-law attorneys to use it as a mediation-lite deliverable and convert 5 of them to paid. Time-box the whole thing to about three weeks per estate.

title: Brewery Tank-Time for Fermentation Startups
one_liner: Rent the empty fermenters of struggling craft breweries to early-stage fermentation companies that cannot get pilot-scale capacity, with standard SOPs and insurance.
customer: Buyers: seed-to-Series-A companies making probiotics and postbiotics, lactic-acid-bacteria and yeast-based ingredients, cultured foods, kombucha-adjacent drinks and biocontrol products that need 1 to 30 kL runs. Sellers: craft breweries, cideries and distilleries with idle tanks.
problem: Pilot-scale food-grade fermentation capacity is scarce and expensive for startups. Meanwhile the Brewers Association says breweries used only about 55% of capacity in 2024, there were 481 closures against 300 openings in 2025, and US craft breweries fell to 9,344 by June 2026. Neither side knows how to contract safely, and food-safety, TTB and insurance issues block informal deals.
solution: A marketplace with a standardized brewery-as-CDMO package: BSL-1 organism screening, cleaning and changeover SOPs, food-facility registration checks, TTB premises guidance, a template contract and insurer-backed coverage. A rentable clip-on aeration and dissolved-oxygen kit extends tanks to low-aeration aerobic processes. Startups book tank-days and downstream time (centrifuge, filtration, cold room).
why_now: Craft brewing is in a third year of decline, with real estate and tank capacity stranded. Startup funding is tight, so cheap pilot capacity matters. Sensors and remote fermentation monitoring make third-party oversight feasible.
revenue_model: Startups pay $300 to $900 per tank-day; the brewery keeps about 80%, the platform takes 15% to 20%. Fees for SOP set-up, kit rental and insurance referral.
non_obvious_insight: Tanks are not the scarce input; validated protocols and biosafety trust are. Most brewery fermenters are unstirred and anaerobic, so the honest wedge is anaerobic and low-aeration products, with an aeration retrofit unlocking more later. A platform that standardizes the SOP and contract becomes the default channel.
first_30_days: Recruit 8 breweries within a few hours of Boston, the Bay Area or Denver that have idle 10-to-30-barrel fermenters. Work with a food-safety consultant to write a one-organism SOP. Approach 25 fermentation startups and run 3 paid pilot batches at $2k to $5k each.

title: Retrain Displaced Managers for Data-Center Builds
one_liner: A 10-week bridge program that turns laid-off program managers, analysts and ops leads into project-controls, cost-estimating, commissioning-paperwork and permitting roles at data-center and grid builders.
customer: General contractors, EPC firms, data-center developers and utility contractors pay a $12-25k placement fee or staff-augmentation margin. Learners pay little, or the cost is covered by workforce-board funds.
problem: Everyone tells displaced office workers to 'learn AI', the most crowded direction. Meanwhile AI's own physical build-out has a shortage of schedulers (P6), cost engineers, document controllers, commissioning coordinators and interconnection or permit analysts. Contractors can't hire them, and mid-career office workers face 6-13 month searches.
solution: Cohort training on scheduling, cost control, contracts, commissioning documentation and site-safety basics, taught by retired project-controls leads. It includes a paid 4-week job-shadow on live projects, certification prep (OSHA 30, PMI-SP, AACE) and guaranteed interviews with partner contractors.
why_now: Hyperscaler capex on data centers and grid work is at record levels and contractors openly cite labor shortages. Big-company cuts of managers ('anti-bureaucracy' layoffs like Amazon's ~16,000) are pushing experienced coordinators onto the market. Stanford data shows the pain concentrated in AI-exposed office roles.
revenue_model: Placement fee of 10-15% of first-year salary (about $12-18k) from contractors, plus paid corporate cohorts and optional deferred tuition.
non_obvious_insight: The AI boom creates a shortage of non-technical, non-AI office roles in the physical world. The displaced manager's scarce skill (vendor wrangling, org navigation, documentation discipline) is exactly what construction lacks, and nobody is training for it.
first_30_days: Call 20 mid-size mechanical and electrical contractors in hot markets (Texas, Virginia, Ohio, Arizona) and get their unfilled-role lists. Sign 3 pay-per-hire LOIs. Recruit 15 laid-off PMs from layoff communities. Run a 4-week evening pilot with a retired scheduler and place the first 5.

title: Cross-Border Clearinghouse for VTuber Merch
one_liner: A duty-paid storefront and fulfillment rail for VTuber agencies that pre-sells to overseas fans and clears unsold Japanese inventory to them.
customer: Mid-size and independent VTuber and idol agencies (not Cover or Anycolor initially), plus overseas fans buying from a duty-paid storefront.
problem: Cover Corp's FY3/2026 revenue rose 13.7% but net profit fell 45.7%, hit by 1.8B yen of unsold merch and a 3.3B yen metaverse write-off. Overseas viewers are about 30% of viewership and roughly 10B yen of revenue, yet those fans face customs surprises, region-locked stores and 30-100% proxy markups.
solution: A global storefront and fulfillment layer with duty-paid shipping, pre-order demand aggregation, and Japanese warehouse partners. Overseas pre-order counts feed manufacturing quantities to reduce overproduction. Overstock is bought or consigned and resold to overseas fans with authenticity guarantees.
why_now: The US ended its $800 de minimis exemption in Aug 2025 and the EU is moving the same way, which breaks the old cheap-parcel proxy model. Hololive's profit drop is a public case study in overproduction.
revenue_model: 15-25% commission on gross merchandise value plus fulfillment fees, and 25-40% of wholesale margin on bought overstock.
non_obvious_insight: Overproduction in Japan and unmet demand overseas are two sides of one imbalance. Forecasts miss overseas demand because logistics hide it, so a clearinghouse converts waste into revenue and generates a better forecast from pre-orders.
first_30_days: Contact 10 small VTuber agencies and 3 Japanese merch producers. Launch a 50-SKU duty-paid shop for one agency. Line up a Japan-based fulfillment partner and pre-sell to an overseas fan community.

title: Real-Pixel Blink Fixer for Family Formals
one_liner: A Lightroom/Photoshop plugin that turns a 5-frame burst of the 30-person family formal into one frame where every set of eyes is open, using only real pixels from the burst and no generated faces.
customer: Solo and small-studio wedding photographers (roughly 100k in the US), paying $29-49/mo or about $2 per composite. Later extension: school, team, church and corporate group-portrait photographers.
problem: Family formals are the 20-40 minute block of the day that grandparents care about most. They are also mathematically hostile. If each person has their eyes closed about 8% of the time, a 30-person frame has under a 10% chance of everyone being open, before counting people who look away or squint. So the delivered frame is nearly always a compromise or a composite. Photographers either hand-swap heads in Photoshop (20-40 minutes per group, or $15-40 per image if outsourced), ship the frame with the blinker, or use generative fill. Generative fill invents a face, which is a betrayal when the face is a grandfather who won't be there in two years.
solution: Drop in the formals folder. The tool groups frames into bursts, aligns them (people shift between frames), scores each person's face for eyes open, smile, gaze and sharpness, picks the best patch per person, and blends with seam-aware masks. The output is a layered PSD so the photographer can override any face in one click. The pitch is a strict 'zero generative pixels' guarantee. A second mode is a shoot-time phone companion that says 'frame 3 has 2 blinkers, shoot one more' so bursts are captured with enough variety. The wedge is batch mode for formals only, not a full editor.
why_now: Google's Best Take (Pixel 8, 2023) taught consumers to expect a merged best-expression group photo. Photographers already pay monthly for AI culling and editing, so AI tooling is normal spend in this trade. Adobe's own face-swap route leans on generative fill, which many pros distrust for client faces. On-device face-landmark and eye-state models are now cheap and accurate enough to run locally on a laptop. Searches in Sept 2026 found only manual Photoshop tutorials for this, not a dedicated automated burst-composite product.
revenue_model: Subscription of $29/mo for solo shooters or $2 per composite credit with monthly bundles. Studio plans at $79/mo. Optional white-label API for gallery platforms (Pic-Time, ShootProof-type) later.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody outside the trade realizes that a truly 'perfect' 30-person frame almost never exists in a single exposure, so every delivered formal is quietly a fix or a compromise. The fix that matters is provenance: the people who print the formals at 16x20 are the elderly relatives, and they will notice an AI-invented face on Grandpa. 'Real pixels only' is the actual feature, not the face-swapping.
first_30_days: Build against Lightroom Classic/Photoshop with open-source face-landmark models. Ask 20 photographers in Facebook groups and r/WeddingPhotography to send 3 old formals bursts from past weddings (every working shooter has hundreds sitting in archives). Return composites in 24 hours with before/after slider pages. First 10 composites free, then $2 each via Stripe. Post the before/afters and blink-probability math in photographer communities. Goal is 30 paying studios and one gallery-platform partnership conversation by day 90.

title: Film Camera Repair Guild and Parts Mill
one_liner: A training-plus-parts network that multiplies the number of people able to repair 1970s-90s film cameras, using 3D-printed and machined parts and paid video teardown courses.
customer: Independent repair techs and serious hobbyists (parts kits and courses), used-camera shops and labs (bulk repaired-and-warrantied stock), and consumers via mail-in.
problem: The film revival is real but repairers are retiring (ABC News Dec 2025; PetaPixel Jan 2026), many now refuse to service certain models, and mechanical parts are hard to source. Dead cameras mean lost film buyers.
solution: Start with the ~25 most popular bodies (AE-1, K1000, X-700, FM2 and similar). Sell light-seal, mirror-bumper and foam kits plus printed or CNC-machined gears. Publish paid step-by-step repair courses, certify guild repairers, route overflow mail-in jobs to them, and sell warrantied repaired stock wholesale to used shops.
why_now: The retirement wave is now documented in mainstream press. Cheap multi-material printing and on-demand metal parts vendors exist. Film demand keeps rising among under-35s, and used-camera prices are climbing.
revenue_model: Parts kits ($8-40), course subscriptions (~$20/month), a ~25% share of routed repairs, and wholesale of repaired cameras with warranty.
non_obvious_insight: Film-industry insiders assume the constraint on the revival is film stock and new cameras. It is repair capacity: repair knowledge is tacit and walking out the door. Apprenticeship packaged as content, plus a parts supply, is the picks-and-shovels play, and every dead SLR is a lost film customer.
first_30_days: Buy 20 broken AE-1 and K1000 lots on eBay and film every teardown. Sell foam and seal kits on Etsy and eBay with instructions. Pre-sell 100 lifetime course seats to r/AnalogCommunity. Recruit 3 retiring techs as paid instructors on revenue share.

title: Verifier-Ready Emissions Data Rooms for CBAM Exporters
one_liner: A metering-to-evidence pipeline that gives small non-EU steel, aluminum and fertilizer producers a clean, pre-audited data room for accredited verifiers, so their EU and UK buyers stop defaulting to punitive default values.
customer: Producers and processors with 50-500 employees in Turkey, India, Egypt, Vietnam, Ukraine and South Africa (steel re-rollers, extruders, wire and fastener makers, fertilizer blenders). Paid by the producer or subsidized by the EU/UK importer buying from them.
problem: CBAM entered its definitive phase in 2026 and UK CBAM starts 1 Jan 2027 across 8 sectors. Importers lacking actual emissions data fall back on default values, which carry a mark-up (background, verify). Accredited verifiers are scarce, and small producers keep energy invoices in spreadsheets with no monitoring plan, so verification is slow and expensive and importers cannot get usable data.
solution: A two-week onboarding: connect electricity and gas meters or invoices, production logs and precursor traceability, then generate the monitoring methodology plan, the emissions report in CBAM format and an evidence index. Internal pre-verification, hand-off to partner verifiers, quarterly refresh, and sharing of the verified data with each importer through an API.
why_now: The definitive period began in 2026, verification of 2026 imports lands in 2027, and UK CBAM begins in three months. Default-value cost pressure now exceeds the price of proper data collection.
revenue_model: EUR 6-25k/year per plant (producer-paid or importer-sponsored supplier program) plus a coordination fee per verification.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone sells CBAM to the EU importer's finance team. The bottleneck is evidence-poor factories and verifier capacity upstream. Importers will fund supplier readiness because default values cost more than the tool, and verified plant data is reusable across every EU and UK customer of that plant.
first_30_days: Find three EU or UK importers of steel wire or fasteners with Turkish or Indian suppliers (trade fairs, LinkedIn) and offer a supplier-readiness pilot for five plants at EUR 3k each. Deliver with templates and spreadsheets and partner with one or two verifiers.
